<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918549_theRebbe_741" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918549_theRebbe_741__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the above, the praises of Rashbi, such as "He is called Shabbat" and "Who is the Face of the Lord Havayah—that is Rashbi," allude to drawing down the transcendent to the lower realm, and even more so, that this drawing down is achieved through the work of the lower being.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on all the above, this will also be understood: that the praises with which they praised Rashbi</t>
    <t s="2">(as brought in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="3">in order to arouse the influence—"He is called Shabbat, and 'Who is the Face of the Lord Havayah, that is Rashbi'"—</t>
    <t s="4">for in these praises is hinted the drawing down of the Supernal</t>
    <t s="5">(which is incomparably separate)</t>
    <t s="6">below,</t>
    <t s="7">and even more so, that the drawing down is through the work of the lower being.</t>
    <t s="8">For, behold,</t>
    <t s="9">regarding Shabbat it is written,</t>
    <t s="10">"For it is holy,"</t>
    <t s="11">"Holy is an independent entity,"</t>
    <t s="12">meaning that Shabbat is separate and incomparable to the six days of work,</t>
    <t s="13">and nevertheless, the holiness of Shabbat is drawn into the days before it and after it,</t>
    <t s="14">for from the fourth day onward it is before Shabbat, and until the fourth day it is after Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="15">in addition to the fact that from Shabbat all the days are blessed.</t>
    <t s="16">And so too regarding man,</t>
    <t s="17">that despite Shabbat being inherently sanctified,</t>
    <t s="18">since the holiness of Shabbat is a most elevated holiness,</t>
    <t s="19">"Holy is an independent entity"</t>
    <t s="20">(as above),</t>
    <t s="21">it is not subject to the grasp of man's hand,</t>
    <t s="22">nevertheless, power is given to Israel to add to the holiness of Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="23">"Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,"</t>
    <t s="24">to the extent that Israel also adds to the delight of Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="25">as the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="26">"Whoever delights in Shabbat."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly, "Face of the Lord Havayah" refers to the unification of the essential name Havayah with the aspect of Adon, which is the Master over all creations, and in the mitzvah of pilgrimage, seeing God below corresponds directly to seeing above, achieved through this unification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And so too regarding the matter of "Who is the Face of the Lord Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="1">for Havayah is the essential name, the explicit name, and the unique name,</t>
    <t s="2">unlike this, that He is called by the name Adon, as the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="3">"It is fitting for You to be called Adon, for You are Master over all Your creations,"</t>
    <t s="4">in addition to the fact that the name Adon is in the Sefirah of Malchus,</t>
    <t s="5">and in Malchus itself—as it descends into Beriah,</t>
    <t s="6">to bring the worlds into existence and to be Master over them,</t>
    <t s="7">behold, from the language of the Sages, "You are Master over all Your creations"</t>
    <t s="8">(specifically "Your creations")</t>
    <t s="9">implies that the name Adon</t>
    <t s="10">is over these creations that are mere creations</t>
    <t s="11">[and analogous to a master in simple terms,</t>
    <t s="12">that the title master is specifically over slaves].</t>
    <t s="13">And the matter of "the Face of the Lord Havayah" is the unification of Havayah</t>
    <t s="14">(the essential name)</t>
    <t s="15">with the aspect of Adon</t>
    <t s="16">(Master over all Your creations).</t>
    <t s="17">And this is also what is written regarding the mitzvah of pilgrimage,</t>
    <t s="18">"Every male shall see the Face of the Lord Havayah."</t>
    <t s="19">For, behold, the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="20">"Just as he comes to be seen, so he comes to see,"</t>
    <t s="21">for in addition to the fact that during the pilgrimage they saw Divinity tangibly</t>
    <t s="22">(for seeing is above comprehension)</t>
    <t s="23">and the seeing was also in the aspect of the inwardness of Divinity, as it says, "see... the Face of...",</t>
    <t s="24">behold, even more so,</t>
    <t s="25">that man's seeing of Divinity</t>
    <t s="26">(from below to above)</t>
    <t s="27">was in the same manner as the seeing above,</t>
    <t s="28">"Just as he comes to be seen, so he comes to see,"</t>
    <t s="29">"They shall gaze directly upon their face,"</t>
    <t s="30">that the seeing below and the seeing above are direct,</t>
    <t s="31">in equivalence.</t>
    <t s="32">Therefore, it is said regarding this, "see... the Face of the Lord Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="33">for in order for there to be the unification of the seeing below with the seeing above,</t>
    <t s="34">it is through the drawing down of the aspect of the Lord Havayah,</t>
    <t s="35">the unification of Adon with Havayah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Furthermore, the mitzvah of pilgrimage includes bringing a physical offering, specifically from an animal, and through this dross refinement, the revelation of the inwardness of Divinity is achieved in a direct vision.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="1">that in the mitzvah of pilgrimage is included the bringing of an offering</t>
    <t s="2">(the burnt-offering of pilgrimage)</t>
    <t s="3">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="4">"And they shall not appear before Me empty-handed."</t>
    <t s="5">In this is seen the greatness of the elevation of the work of refinement,</t>
    <t s="6">that through bringing a physical offering</t>
    <t s="7">[and according to one opinion,</t>
    <t s="8">the offering must be not from fowl but from an animal],</t>
    <t s="9">specifically through this they shall see the Face,</t>
    <t s="10">the revelation of the inwardness of Divinity and in a manner of seeing,</t>
    <t s="11">even to the aspect of "They shall gaze directly upon their face."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
